text.text_excerpt: I recently attended a wedding here and left declaring it my favorite wedding venue in New Orleans. The space is perfection, if you love the idea of a peaceful, rustic, ecclesiastical ("in spirit"- this is a secular space as far as I could tell) setting that is quintessential NOLA, without being cliché. I love how the ceremony took place in the actual church space upstairs, then you moved on downstairs to a nice space and the courtyard for the cocktail hour and then... the church is magically transformed into magical event space! I always thought it would be cool for a reception to take place in a church and kinda never thought it could happen (hello, I was raised Catholic). Here, this is ...

I couldn't believe my lucky stars when Robert and I confirmed Felicity Church for November 11, 2017. I had never planned on getting married in a "church". My dream was to marry on a beach with my toes in the sand or surrounded by beautiful flowers in a garden pungent with the scent of blooming jasmines. With the wild inconsistency of New Orleans weather, plans change. More to kickstart my venue hunt, I booked viewings at a number of places as well as Felicity Church in the summer of 2016. While I've enjoyed beautiful weddings at The Elms Mansion, Latrobe's, and Rosy's Jazz Hall, I wanted something different as most any bride would. Felicity Church hadn't been an official venue for that lo...

I work as a wedding planner and I have had the joy of having 4 couples select Felicity church for their nuptials or their reception. It is truly one of the most beautiful spaces in the city to get married. Chris (the owner) and his wife are very sweet and accommodating. They can transform the space from a typical church layout to the ultimate party space. I think this is very cool because you can get married and have the reception in the same location but with a totally different fun feel for the reception. If I ever get married I would chose Felicity Church over most of the other venues I have worked at in the city. That says a lot!
